Subject: ACME POC: Integration plan & trial success criteria

Hi Tara / Ben,

Thanks for the call earlier — great to meet the ACME team. Per our discussion, here's a proposed plan for the 2-week POC / trial and integration checklist so we can validate the model in your workflow.

POC timeline
- Start: 2026-03-23
- Duration: 2 weeks (23 Mar - 6 Apr)

Success criteria (candidate)
1) Latency: median inference latency < 200ms for 512-token requests in your US region
2) Throughput: sustain 50 concurrent requests with 95th perc latency < 500ms
3) Quality: >= 85% accuracy on your golden prompt set (we'll run automated evals)
4) Stability: no production-impacting errors; <0.1% 5xx rate

Evaluation plan
- Week 0 (pre-POC): integration & sample data import, baseline tests
- Week 1: run streaming & batch tests, collect metrics, tweak batching/quant
- Week 2: run gold-set evals, hand-off for UAT

Owners & next steps
- ACME dev lead: Tara Singh — integration & test data
- Redwood SE: Dev Patel (cc'd) — SDK support, API routing
- Redwood AE: Marissa Cole — commercial / timelines

Tech items to validate
- SDK: Python & Node quickstart
- API routes: /v1/generate (sync), /v1/stream (server-sent events), function/tool calling for structured actions
- Authentication via API keys + optional mTLS for Private deployments

I've attached a short POC plan doc for your review (acme-poc-plan.pdf). Can we confirm the start date 2026-03-23? Also propose a 30-minute tech sync with Dev on Mon 2026-03-22.

Thanks,

—

Thanks Tara — adding Dev to handle the integration details. Quick answers below and Dev will drop a short integration checklist and example calls before the sync.

- Streaming: /v1/stream supports incremental token deltas via SSE and WebSocket; reconnect uses last-event-id semantics and we provide chunked tokens + approximate token indexes.

- Function/tool calling: the runtime emits a structured JSON payload for function calls (name, arguments, call_id). For streaming, you'll receive a "tool_call_initiated" event followed by arguments and then "tool_call_result". We include call_id so you can correlate. Dev can show a sample.

- SDKs: Python & Node quickstarts available; Python SDK includes built-in retry/backoff and helpers for streaming consumption.

- Security: attaching our SOC 2 summary and options for IP allowlist / mTLS. For Private deployments we can swap the auth to your IdP-backed tokens.

Hi Tara / Ben — happy to take the tech sync. Below is a concise integration checklist and sample calls to get you started; I'll bring live examples to the sync.

Integration checklist (first-pass)
- Create Redwood API key scoped to POC environment
- Install Python SDK (pip install redwood-sdk) or use REST endpoints
- Import your golden prompt set to S3 (we can pull from a shared folder)
- Implement streaming client (SSE or WebSocket) with reconnect and last-event-id
- Wire tool-calling endpoint (POST /internal/tool-result) to accept call_id and result payloads
- Run baseline latency/throughput tests (see below)

Recommended endpoints
- Sync generate: POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  payload: {"model":"redwood-v1.2","input":"...","max_tokens":512}
- Streaming (SSE): GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream?model=redwood-v1.2&session_id=<uuid>
  semantics: sends events: event: token_delta, data: {"token":"...","index":123} and event: tool_call_initiated/data: {"call_id":"...","name":"resolve_entity","args":{...}}
- Function/tool result POST: POST https://api.redwood.ai/internal/tool-result
  payload: {"call_id":"...","status":"ok","result":{...}}

Sample Python SDK snippet

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<REDACTED>")
# sync
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-v1.2", input="Summarize the following...", max_tokens=256)
print(resp.text)

# streaming (async example)
async for chunk in client.stream(model="redwood-v1.2", input="Explain X", session_id="acme-poc"):
    if chunk.type == 'token_delta':
        print(chunk.token, end='')
    elif chunk.type == 'tool_call_initiated':
        # call your service and then post result to Redwood
        result = call_internal_service(chunk.args)
        client.post_tool_result(call_id=chunk.call_id, result=result)

Performance knobs & recommendations
- Use dynamic batching: set batch_size=16 for peak throughput tests
- Enable KV prefix cache for repeated customer prompts to reduce latency
- Quantization: we recommend 4/8-bit profile for cost saving if you see no quality regression
- Rate limits for POC: 60 req/s default; we can raise for the test window if needed

I'll attach an integration checklist CSV and bring sample curl and SDK demos to the sync. Confirming the tech-sync Mon 2026-03-22 10:00 PT — I'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
—
Dev Patel
